title: Privacy, worth doing soon: reminders keep arriving that the screen says are off; the email's unsubscribe link is the person's only way out
evidence: PR 1 held (2221, 2026-11-27): health-core merges the opt-in per token (packages/health-core/src/reminder-rows.ts: rowsOf, mergeOptIn, shownOptIn; merge.ts calls mergeOptIn), migrate validates and sanitizes the nested rows, a file with tokens rows is stamped at least version 2, the check after a save covers the opt-in, and setReminderRow (state-edits.ts) writes one row (US-17 AC19, US-32 AC67). PR 2 held (PR2NUM, 2026-11-27, merges with 2221): every web writer goes through setReminderRow in one guarded edit (widget-src/standalone/reminders.ts; the switch writes the old token cancelled with the new one; a 404 cancels the pushed token only); Turn off cancels every token as one TurnOff state (widget-src/standalone/reminders-turn-off.ts, per-row unchanged-since check); the control shows every active address (reminders-control.tsx); visibleContentOf announces a change to the shown row or the active addresses; the erase hands the teardown every copy it read at its swap (EraseSteps.swapping, record-session-erase.ts) and spares tokens active in any row of the standing record (reminders-erase-cancel.ts); erase.ts strips tokens in its provider tie-break; the state-edits setReminderOptIn writer is deleted (US-17 AC19 extended, US-11 AC15, AC17 Limit trimmed). Design: docs/drafts/r9-optin-cancel-merge-design.md. Root fix R9 (triage 2026-11-25): opt-in merge: a cancel beats an active opt-in only for its own token. Residual of H18e (US-17 AC17 Limit). Device A taps Turn off on active T1 while device B turns reminders on (Drive: A's cancel deletes the row, B inserts T2 and writes active T2). If A has not merged B's write before its own (the usual case: the 60 s poll, REMOTE_POLL_MS, packages/health-core/src/record-session.ts:38), A's cancelled T1 carries the later stamp and wins the opt-in merge (pickNewerOptional, packages/health-core/src/merge.ts:389, applied at :856; time first then lamport, cmpClock :423-427). End: the record says cancelled T1 on every device, the server row T2 stays live, pushes stop, and no Turn off in the app reaches T2. The fix is merge-level: a cancel beats an active opt-in only for its own token. A naive rule is not associative, so devices can diverge: aT2(t1), aT1(t3), cT1(t4) merge to cT1 one way and aT1 the other. Design note with a convergence proof first; merge semantics, health-core, engine release. Source: the H18e design note (Option C).
